nodes.name: Supertrend
nodes.what_it_does: A single ATR-offset trailing line that sits below price in an uptrend and above price in a downtrend, flipping side when a close crosses it. Used as a trend-direction filter and as a volatility-scaled trailing stop. No peer-reviewed evidence of standalone edge; its value in systems is mostly as a regime/stop component.
nodes.core_math: Midpoint hl2 plus/minus multiplier x ATR(n) gives basic upper/lower bands. Bands ratchet: the lower band may only rise (unless the prior close broke below it) and the upper band may only fall (unless the prior close broke above it). Direction flips when close crosses the active band; the plotted line is the lower band in uptrend and upper band in downtrend. Typical defaults ATR 10, factor 3.
nodes.outputs: One line colored by direction; flip points used as buy/sell signals.
nodes.timeframes: All; intraday use on NQ/ES typically 1-15m with higher factors to cut whipsaw
nodes.repaints: no - uses closed-bar values; the live bar can flip intrabar before close if signals are taken on tick
nodes.weaknesses: Whipsaws badly in ranges; lagging entries give back a lot on reversal; parameter-sensitive. No published robust evidence specific to Supertrend; generic trend-following evidence (Moskowitz et al.) is at monthly horizons, not intraday.

nodes.name: Chandelier Exit
nodes.source: Charles Le Beau (origin), Alexander Elder (popularized); everget (TradingView)
nodes.license: TradingView House Rules (open-source; license header unknown)
nodes.what_it_does: An ATR trailing stop hung from the highest high (for longs) or lowest low (for shorts) of a lookback window. everget's version tracks long/short state and marks flips as signals. Primarily an exit/stop tool rather than an entry edge.
nodes.core_math: Long stop = highest high (or highest close, option) over n bars minus k x ATR(n); short stop = lowest low over n minus k x ATR(n). Long stop is ratcheted up only while the prior close stays above it; direction flips when close crosses the opposite stop. Common defaults n=22, k=3.
nodes.outputs: Long and short stop lines, buy/sell flip labels, optional state highlighting and alerts (with bar-confirmation option).
nodes.repaints: no - based on closed-bar extremes; alerts have a confirm-on-close option
nodes.weaknesses: Same whipsaw profile as Supertrend (mechanically very similar, anchored to extremes instead of midpoint). No specific published evidence of edge; useful as risk management.

nodes.name: Donchian Channel Breakout / Turtle Trading System
nodes.source: Richard Donchian; Richard Dennis & William Eckhardt (Turtles); Curtis Faith (rules published)
nodes.what_it_does: Channel of the highest high and lowest low over N bars; buying a break of the N-bar high and shorting a break of the N-bar low. The Turtle rules add two entry systems, a skip rule, ATR-based sizing, stops and pyramiding. Trading-range-break rules were among those found significant by Brock, Lakonishok & LeBaron (1992) on 90 years of DJIA data.
nodes.core_math: Upper = highest high(N), lower = lowest low(N), mid = average. Turtle System 1: enter on 20-day breakout, skip if last System 1 signal in the same direction was a winner; exit on 10-day opposite breakout. System 2: 55-day breakout, 20-day exit. N = 20-day exponential average of true range; unit size set so 1 N move = 1% of equity; stop at 2N; add units every 0.5N up to limits.
nodes.outputs: Upper/lower/middle channel; breakout entries and channel exits.
nodes.timeframes: Designed for daily futures; intraday versions exist but evidence is daily/multi-day
nodes.repaints: no - uses prior completed bars' extremes (with offset 1); breakouts can trigger intrabar
nodes.weaknesses: Low win rate, long flat/drawdown periods, heavy dependence on rare big trends. BLL (1992) evidence is on daily DJIA pre-1987 and weakened in later samples (Sullivan, Timmermann & White found data-snooping-adjusted significance fades post-1986). Intraday edge on index futures not established.

nodes.name: Bollinger Bands (with %b and BandWidth)
nodes.what_it_does: A moving average with bands a fixed number of standard deviations above and below, adapting to realized volatility. Used for mean reversion (fade band touches), breakout/trend (band walks) and volatility contraction (BandWidth lows). Derived tools %b and BandWidth normalize position and width.
nodes.core_math: Basis = SMA(close, 20); upper/lower = basis +/- 2 x population stdev(close, 20). %b = (close - lower)/(upper - lower). BandWidth = (upper - lower)/basis. A squeeze is a BandWidth near its lookback minimum.
nodes.outputs: Three bands; %b and BandWidth oscillators.
nodes.repaints: no - rolling window on closed bars
nodes.weaknesses: Directionally ambiguous (same touch can mean reversion or breakout); stdev assumes a stationary distribution. No robust academic evidence of standalone profitability; results in backtests are strongly regime-dependent.

nodes.name: Keltner Channels
nodes.source: Chester Keltner (original); Linda Bradford Raschke (EMA/ATR version); TradingView built-in
nodes.what_it_does: An EMA envelope offset by a multiple of ATR, giving smoother, less spiky bands than Bollinger. Used for breakout (close outside band) or pullback-to-basis trend entries, and as the reference envelope in the TTM squeeze.
nodes.core_math: Basis = EMA(close, 20); upper/lower = basis +/- 2 x ATR (built-in default ATR length 14; band style may alternatively be true range or high-low range).
nodes.outputs: Three lines; breakout signals in the built-in Keltner Channels Strategy.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: No specific published evidence of edge. ATR-based width reacts slower than stdev bands to volatility shocks.

nodes.name: TTM Squeeze / Squeeze Momentum Indicator
nodes.source: John Carter (TTM Squeeze, 'Mastering the Trade' ch. 11); LazyBear (TradingView port)
nodes.what_it_does: Flags volatility compression when Bollinger Bands contract inside Keltner Channels, then signals the 'fire' when they expand back out, with a momentum histogram giving direction. Built on the volatility-clustering idea that quiet periods precede expansions. LazyBear's version is one of the most-used scripts on TradingView.
nodes.core_math: Squeeze on when BB(20, 2.0 sd) upper < KC(20, 1.5 x range) upper and BB lower > KC lower; off when BB moves back outside KC. LazyBear's momentum: linear-regression value (length 20) of close minus the average of (Donchian midpoint of the window and SMA of close) - a linreg-based substitute for Carter's momentum. Histogram shade shows rising/falling momentum.
nodes.outputs: Zero-line dots (squeeze on/off/none) and colored momentum histogram.
nodes.repaints: no - on closed bars; histogram color can change intrabar
nodes.weaknesses: Squeeze tells timing of expansion, not direction; momentum direction at the fire is often wrong in chop. Volatility clustering itself is well documented (GARCH literature), but no published evidence that the squeeze trigger is profitable after costs.

nodes.name: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo (Ichimoku Cloud)
nodes.what_it_does: A complete trend system of five lines built from midpoints of high/low ranges, including a forward-shifted 'cloud' used as support/resistance and trend state. Signals come from Tenkan/Kijun crosses, price vs. cloud and cloud color.
nodes.core_math: Tenkan = (HH+LL)/2 over 9; Kijun = (HH+LL)/2 over 26; Senkou A = (Tenkan+Kijun)/2 plotted 26 bars ahead; Senkou B = (HH+LL)/2 over 52 plotted 26 ahead; Chikou = close plotted 26 bars back.
nodes.outputs: Five lines and the shaded cloud between Senkou A and B.
nodes.timeframes: Designed for daily; used on all
nodes.repaints: no for calculations; Chikou is displayed shifted back so visual reading of it at the current bar implies look-ahead if misused in backtests
nodes.weaknesses: Many lagging midpoints; the 9/26/52 constants come from a 6-day trading week and are arbitrary intraday. Little rigorous evidence; some academic tests on equities/FX show mixed, mostly insignificant results after costs.

nodes.name: Parabolic SAR
nodes.source: J. Welles Wilder Jr. (1978); TradingView built-in
nodes.what_it_does: A stop-and-reverse trailing stop that accelerates toward price as the trend makes new extremes, so it is always in the market long or short. Mostly used as a trailing stop.
nodes.core_math: SAR_next = SAR + AF x (EP - SAR), where EP is the extreme point of the current trend. AF starts at 0.02, rises by 0.02 at each new EP, capped at 0.20. SAR may not move inside the prior two bars' range. When price crosses SAR, the position reverses, SAR resets to the prior EP and AF resets.
nodes.outputs: Dots above/below price; reversal points.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Always-in-market design produces constant whipsaws in ranges. No robust evidence of edge.

nodes.name: ADX / Directional Movement Index (DMI)
nodes.source: J. Welles Wilder Jr. (1978); TradingView built-in
nodes.what_it_does: Measures trend direction (+DI vs -DI) and trend strength regardless of direction (ADX). Most useful as a regime filter: trade trend systems when ADX is high/rising and mean-reversion when low.
nodes.core_math: +DM = up-move if it exceeds down-move and >0, else 0; -DM symmetric. Wilder-smooth +DM, -DM and true range over n (14); +DI = 100 x sm(+DM)/sm(TR), -DI likewise. DX = 100 x |+DI - -DI|/(+DI + -DI); ADX = Wilder smoothing of DX.
nodes.outputs: +DI, -DI and ADX lines; common threshold ADX > 20-25 = trending.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Double smoothing makes ADX very laggy - it peaks after trends are mature. No strong published evidence; used as a filter inside systems (e.g. the ADX filter in jdehorty's Lorentzian classifier).

nodes.name: Session VWAP with Standard Deviation Bands
nodes.what_it_does: The cumulative volume-weighted average price since the session (or other anchor period) start, with bands at multiples of the volume-weighted standard deviation. Serves as the intraday fair-value reference that execution algos benchmark against, so it acts as a magnet and a trend-bias line on NQ/ES.
nodes.core_math: Typical price = hlc3; VWAP = cumulative(tp x volume)/cumulative(volume), reset at each anchor (Session/Week/Month/..., or earnings/dividends/splits). Bands = VWAP +/- k x standard deviation of prices around VWAP since the anchor (three user multipliers; percentage mode available).
nodes.outputs: VWAP line and up to three band pairs.
nodes.timeframes: Intraday (1m-30m) on session anchor; weekly/monthly anchors for swing
nodes.repaints: no - cumulative and forward-only; the live bar's value updates until close
nodes.weaknesses: Anchor choice matters for futures (RTH vs. ETH session). Its fair-value/benchmark role is real (execution literature), but trading edge comes from the rule built around it - see the VWAP trend node.

nodes.name: VWAP Trend Trading (Zarattini & Aziz)
nodes.what_it_does: A simple intraday regime rule: be long when price is above session VWAP and short when below, trading only during regular hours and flat overnight. The paper reports on QQQ 2018-2023 a 671% return net of commissions, max drawdown 9.4%, Sharpe about 2.1, and much larger numbers on TQQQ.
nodes.core_math: On intraday bars (the paper uses 1-minute), compute session VWAP; hold long when close > VWAP, short when close < VWAP, flip on crossings, close all at session end.
nodes.outputs: Long/short/flat state and flip trades.
nodes.timeframes: Intraday 1m (paper); likely degrades with slower bars
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Single-author-team, in-sample study over a strong trending period (2018-2023) for Nasdaq; frequent flips make it very sensitive to slippage and spread; no independent out-of-sample replication found. Treat as promising but unverified.

nodes.name: Anchored VWAP (manual and auto-anchored)
nodes.source: Brian Shannon (popularized); TradingView drawing tool and VWAP Auto Anchored built-in
nodes.what_it_does: VWAP started from a chosen event bar (swing high/low, gap, news, session open) instead of a calendar reset, giving the average cost of everyone who traded since that event. Price reclaiming or losing an event-anchored VWAP is read as control shifting between buyers and sellers.
nodes.core_math: Same cumulative tp x volume / volume as VWAP, but accumulation begins at the anchor bar; optional standard deviation bands. Auto-anchored variants choose anchors algorithmically (e.g. highest/lowest bar of a period).
nodes.outputs: An AVWAP curve (plus bands) per anchor.
nodes.repaints: conditional - fixed anchors do not repaint; auto-anchors that move to a new high/low redraw from the new anchor
nodes.weaknesses: Anchor selection is discretionary; no rigorous published evidence of edge.

nodes.name: Volume Profile (Session / Fixed Range / Visible Range) with POC and Value Area
nodes.source: Market Profile tradition (Steidlmayer / CBOT); TradingView built-ins
nodes.what_it_does: A horizontal histogram of traded volume by price over a period. The Point of Control (highest-volume row) and the 70% Value Area (VAH/VAL) are used as acceptance/rejection levels; low-volume nodes are expected to be traversed quickly and high-volume nodes to attract price.
nodes.core_math: Split the period's price range into rows (by count or ticks per row); assign each bar's volume to rows it spans (TradingView uses lower-timeframe intrabars to allocate volume and to split up/down volume). POC = max-volume row. Value area: start at POC, repeatedly add the larger of the next row above or below until 70% of total volume is included; top = VAH, bottom = VAL.
nodes.outputs: Histogram, POC, VAH, VAL, often split into up/down volume.
nodes.timeframes: Intraday sessions for NQ/ES (RTH/ETH); composite multi-day profiles
nodes.repaints: conditional - the developing (current session) profile changes until the session ends; completed profiles are fixed
nodes.weaknesses: Bar-based allocation is an approximation of true tick-level volume-at-price. Widely used by futures traders but no peer-reviewed evidence that POC/VA levels predict reversals better than random levels.

nodes.name: TPO / Market Profile
nodes.source: J. Peter Steidlmayer (CBOT, 1980s); TradingView built-in TPO indicator
nodes.what_it_does: Builds a profile of time spent at each price by stacking one letter per price row per time block (e.g. 30 minutes). Identifies balance vs. imbalance, the time-based POC, value area, initial balance and single prints. Complements volume profile with time-at-price.
nodes.core_math: Divide the period into equal time blocks, each assigned a letter; for each block mark every price row its range touched. POC = row with most TPOs; value area = ~70% of TPOs built outward from POC; initial balance = range of the first block(s); single prints = non-extreme rows with one TPO.
nodes.outputs: Letter profile, POC, VAH/VAL, IB range, single prints.
nodes.timeframes: Intraday sessions; daily profiles for NQ/ES
nodes.repaints: conditional - developing profile changes during the session; TradingView alerts fire only on completed profiles
nodes.weaknesses: Interpretive framework (Dalton's day types) is largely discretionary; no rigorous public evidence of edge.

nodes.name: Initial Balance (IB) and IB Extensions
nodes.what_it_does: The high-low range of the first hour of the regular session (first two 30-minute periods). Breaks and failures of IB high/low, and multiples of IB width (1.5x, 2x) are used as intraday targets and day-type classifiers (e.g. narrow IB suggests trend day potential).
nodes.core_math: IB high/low = max/min of price during the first N minutes of RTH (commonly 60). Extensions = IB high + m x IB range and IB low - m x IB range. Classification rules compare IB width to its recent average.
nodes.outputs: Horizontal IB high/low, midpoint and extension levels.
nodes.repaints: no after the IB period closes; levels are provisional during the first hour
nodes.weaknesses: No academic evidence; it is conceptually a 60-minute opening range, so ORB evidence is the closest proxy. Popular claims about IB-extension hit rates are unverified.

nodes.name: Opening Range Breakout (ORB)
nodes.source: Toby Crabel (1990); Zarattini & Aziz, SSRN 4416622; Holmberg, Lonnbark & Lundstrom (2013)
nodes.what_it_does: Trades in the direction price leaves the range formed in the first minutes of the session. Among the best-documented intraday rules: Holmberg et al. (Finance Research Letters 2013) found ORB returns significantly above zero on crude oil futures; Lundstrom later found ORB profitability rises with volatility (including S&P 500 futures); Zarattini & Aziz report +0.13R per trade on QQQ 2016-2023 for a 5-minute version.
nodes.core_math: Opening range = high/low of the first N minutes. Classic: stop orders a fixed distance or at the range extreme. Zarattini-Aziz 5-min variant: take the direction of the first 5-minute candle, enter at the open of the second, stop at the other end of the first candle, target 10R or exit at close. Crabel adds a 'stretch' (average open-to-extreme distance) and volatility-contraction filters (NR4/NR7, inside days).
nodes.outputs: OR high/low levels; long/short entries, stop, target.
nodes.repaints: no once the range period ends
nodes.weaknesses: Zarattini-Aziz charges commissions but no spread/slippage and has no out-of-sample period; an independent replication on five indices reports the gross result reproduces but net returns are near zero (mql5 blog, Sept 2026). The strongest version in their follow-up (SSRN 4729284) relies on 'stocks in play' selection, not applicable to index futures. Evidence is real but thin after costs.

nodes.name: Intraday Momentum 'Noise Area' Breakout (Beat the Market)
nodes.source: Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon, SSRN 4824172 / SFI RP 24-97 (2024)
nodes.what_it_does: Defines a time-of-day-specific 'noise area' around the open from recent days' typical moves and goes with price only when it escapes that band, using VWAP/boundary trailing stops and volatility-targeted sizing. Reported on SPY 2007-2024: 19.6% annualized, Sharpe 1.33 net of costs. An independent test on ES/NQ futures (Quantitativo, with modified 90-day lookback) reported Sharpe 1.25 (ES) and 1.67 (NQ).
nodes.core_math: For each minute-of-day t, sigma_t = average over the last 14 days of |price at t / session open - 1|. Upper = max(open, prior close) x (1 + sigma_t); lower = min(open, prior close) x (1 - sigma_t) (gap-adjusted). Check signals at fixed intervals (half-hour marks in the paper); long above upper, short below lower. Trailing stop = the more protective of the boundary and VWAP. Size to a daily vol target (2%, max 4x leverage in paper). Flat at close. (Parameter details from paper summaries; verify against the PDF before coding.)
nodes.outputs: Time-varying upper/lower boundaries, entries, VWAP/boundary stop.
nodes.repaints: no - boundaries use only prior days and the current open
nodes.weaknesses: Author-published with in-sample design choices; win rate is low (~36-38%) and expectancy per trade small (+2 to +6 bps on ES/NQ per Quantitativo), so costs matter. Independent replications broadly confirm, making this one of the better-evidenced intraday index rules. Mechanism is consistent with intraday momentum literature (Gao et al.; Baltussen et al.).

nodes.name: Market Intraday Momentum (first half-hour predicts last half-hour)
nodes.source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou, Journal of Financial Economics (2018); Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens, JFE (2021)
nodes.what_it_does: Academic finding that the market's return from the prior close through the first 30 minutes (Gao et al.) or over the rest of the day (Baltussen et al.) positively predicts the return in the last 30 minutes. Baltussen et al. confirm it across 60+ futures (equities, bonds, commodities, FX) 1974-2020 and link it to gamma-hedging demand by option market makers and leveraged ETFs.
nodes.core_math: Compute r_early = return from prior close to 10:00 ET (Gao) or open-to-15:30 (Baltussen); at 15:30 take a position in sign(r_early) and exit at the close. Predictability stronger on volatile, high-volume, and macro-news days, and when dealers are net short gamma.
nodes.outputs: End-of-day directional signal.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Peer-reviewed and replicated across assets - among the strongest evidence in this catalog - but per-trade returns are small, so futures (low cost) are the right vehicle. Effect partially reverts over following days. Some later studies find it weaker in recent samples.

nodes.name: Time-Series Momentum (Trend Following)
nodes.source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen, JFE (2012); Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen, JPM (2017)
nodes.what_it_does: Go long an asset whose own past return over a lookback is positive and short if negative, sized by inverse volatility. Documented in all 58 liquid futures studied (1-12 month persistence, partial reversal later) and positive in every decade since 1880. For an intraday NQ/ES algo it is best used as a higher-timeframe bias filter.
nodes.core_math: Signal = sign(return over past k months, classic k=12); position = signal x (target vol / ex-ante realized vol, e.g. exponentially weighted daily vol).
nodes.outputs: Directional bias and position size.
nodes.timeframes: Daily to monthly (evidence); use as HTF filter intraday
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Evidence is at monthly horizons; transferring to intraday is an assumption. Trend-following had a long weak stretch in the 2010s. Strong, peer-reviewed evidence at its native horizon.

nodes.name: Moving Average Crossover Rules (Brock-Lakonishok-LeBaron)
nodes.source: Classic; Brock, Lakonishok & LeBaron, Journal of Finance (1992)
nodes.what_it_does: Buy when a short moving average (or price) crosses above a long one, sell on the reverse, optionally with a percentage band filter. BLL found buy signals from such rules on the DJIA 1897-1986 produced significantly higher returns than sell signals, inconsistent with random walk, AR(1) and GARCH nulls (bootstrap tests).
nodes.core_math: Signal when MA(short) - MA(long) changes sign (BLL used 1/50, 1/150, 5/150, 1/200, 2/200 day pairs with 0% or 1% bands, variable- and fixed-length holding).
nodes.outputs: Long/short state or crossover events.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Later work (Sullivan, Timmermann & White 1999; Park & Irwin 2007 review) shows the effect weakens post-1986 and after data-snooping adjustment; transaction costs were not included in BLL. Historically important, currently weak evidence for index futures intraday.

nodes.name: Floor Pivot Points (Traditional, Fibonacci, Woodie, Classic, DeMark, Camarilla)
nodes.source: Floor-trader classic; TradingView 'Pivot Points Standard' built-in
nodes.what_it_does: Static support/resistance levels computed from the prior period's high, low and close, widely watched by floor and retail traders (hence possibly self-fulfilling). Osler (NY Fed, 2000) showed published S/R levels predicted intraday FX trend interruptions better than random levels, though not these specific formulas.
nodes.core_math: Traditional: P = (H+L+C)/3 of prior period; R1 = 2P - L, S1 = 2P - H; higher levels extend by the range. Camarilla: levels = prior close +/- 1.1 x (H-L)/k with k = 12, 6, 4, 2 for levels 1-4. Other variants reweight open/close.
nodes.outputs: Horizontal P, R1-R5, S1-S5 levels per period.
nodes.timeframes: Intraday using daily pivots; weekly/monthly pivots for swing
nodes.repaints: no - based on the completed prior period
nodes.weaknesses: Direct evidence for pivot formulas is anecdotal; Osler's evidence is about professional S/R levels in FX and varied by firm and currency. For futures, the choice of session (RTH vs. ETH) for H/L/C changes levels.

nodes.name: Heikin Ashi
nodes.source: Japanese charting method; TradingView chart type
nodes.what_it_does: A smoothed candle representation that averages price so trends appear as runs of same-colored candles with no opposing wicks. Used as a trend-visualization or filtering layer, not a separate edge.
nodes.core_math: HA close = (O+H+L+C)/4; HA open = (prior HA open + prior HA close)/2; HA high = max(H, HA open, HA close); HA low = min(L, HA open, HA close).
nodes.outputs: Synthetic candles; color-run and wickless-candle signals.
nodes.repaints: no, but HA prices are synthetic: backtests that fill at HA open/close (TradingView strategy on HA chart without real-OHLC fills) give falsely optimistic results
nodes.weaknesses: No evidence of edge; the classic trap is backtesting on HA chart prices. Adds lag equivalent to a short moving average.

nodes.name: Cumulative Volume Delta (CVD, intrabar approximation)
nodes.what_it_does: Running total of estimated buy volume minus sell volume, reset each anchor period, displayed as candles. Divergence between price and CVD (e.g. new price high without new CVD high) is read as absorption/exhaustion. On TradingView it is an approximation because true bid/ask aggressor data is not used.
nodes.core_math: For each chart bar, iterate over lower-timeframe intrabars: intrabar volume is positive if close > open, negative if close < open; if equal, compare with prior intrabar close, and if also equal inherit the previous classification (tick-rule style). Bar delta = sum; CVD accumulates deltas from the anchor (e.g. session) start.
nodes.outputs: CVD candles; per-bar delta.
nodes.repaints: conditional - depends on intrabar data availability; historical intrabar depth is limited so older bars may be computed differently from live
nodes.weaknesses: Candle-direction classification is a crude proxy for aggressor side (true delta needs tick data with bid/ask). No published evidence that this approximation carries edge; academic order-flow imbalance evidence (e.g. Cont et al.) uses real order-book data.

nodes.name: Delta Volume Profile [BigBeluga]
nodes.license: TradingView House Rules (open-source; header license unknown, BigBeluga scripts commonly CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 - unverified)
nodes.what_it_does: Builds two horizontal volume profiles over a lookback, one from bullish candles and one from bearish candles, to show where buying vs. selling volume concentrated by price, with separate POCs and delta dominance.
nodes.core_math: Bin price range into rows; add each bullish-candle's volume to the bull profile and each bearish-candle's volume to the bear profile at the rows it covers; delta per row = bull - bear; mark POCs of each side. (Exact allocation method not verified.)
nodes.outputs: Twin profiles, POCs, delta annotations.
nodes.repaints: conditional - rolling lookback profile redraws each bar
nodes.weaknesses: Candle color as buy/sell proxy is crude; no evidence of edge.

nodes.name: Kaufman Adaptive Moving Average (KAMA)
nodes.what_it_does: An EMA whose smoothing constant scales with the Efficiency Ratio, so it hugs price in clean trends and nearly freezes in chop. Reduces whipsaw compared with fixed-length MAs.
nodes.core_math: ER = |close - close[n]| / sum(|close - close[1]|, n). SC = (ER x (2/(fast+1) - 2/(slow+1)) + 2/(slow+1))^2 with defaults n=10, fast=2, slow=30. KAMA = KAMA[1] + SC x (close - KAMA[1]).
nodes.outputs: Adaptive MA line; slope/cross signals.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Flat in chop can still be crossed repeatedly by price. No academic evidence of edge; value is mainly noise suppression.

nodes.name: Jurik Moving Average (JMA, community reproduction)
nodes.license: TradingView House Rules (open-source reproduction; original JMA is proprietary)
nodes.what_it_does: A low-lag, low-overshoot adaptive smoother. The original algorithm is commercial and undisclosed; everget's script is an openly published reproduction that the author says differs slightly but behaves like the original in most cases.
nodes.core_math: Reproductions use a volatility-adaptive exponent (relative volatility of recent bands) driving a multi-stage exponential filter, with Phase (-100..100) shifting between lag and overshoot and Power controlling smoothing. Exact original math unknown; community versions vary.
nodes.outputs: Smoothed line; color by slope.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Not the verified original algorithm; claims of superiority come from the vendor. No independent evidence of trading edge.

nodes.name: MESA Adaptive Moving Average (MAMA / FAMA)
nodes.what_it_does: Adapts an EMA's alpha to the rate of change of cycle phase measured with a Hilbert transform, so it ratchets quickly in trends and holds in cycles. FAMA is a slower companion; MAMA/FAMA crosses are intended to mark major turns only.
nodes.core_math: Hilbert transform discriminator on smoothed price gives in-phase and quadrature components, from which phase is computed. deltaPhase = phase[1] - phase (floored at 1). alpha = FastLimit / deltaPhase clamped to [SlowLimit, FastLimit] (defaults 0.5 / 0.05). MAMA = alpha x price + (1-alpha) x MAMA[1]; FAMA = 0.5 alpha x MAMA + (1 - 0.5 alpha) x FAMA[1].
nodes.outputs: MAMA and FAMA lines; crosses.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Phase measurement is noisy on real data; alpha can jump erratically. Evidence is the author's illustrative examples, not independent tests.

nodes.name: Ehlers SuperSmoother (and Roofing / Ultimate Smoother family)
nodes.source: John Ehlers ('Cycle Analytics for Traders', mesasoftware papers)
nodes.what_it_does: A two-pole low-pass filter derived from a Butterworth design that removes high-frequency noise with less lag than an equivalent SMA/EMA. Used as a baseline, and combined with a high-pass filter as a 'roofing filter' to isolate a band of cycle periods before computing oscillators.
nodes.core_math: a1 = exp(-1.414 pi / P); b1 = 2 a1 cos(1.414 pi / P) (radians); c2 = b1; c3 = -a1^2; c1 = 1 - c2 - c3. Filt = c1 x (price + price[1])/2 + c2 x Filt[1] + c3 x Filt[2]. Roofing = high-pass (removes periods > long cutoff) followed by SuperSmoother (removes periods < short cutoff). UltimateSmoother is a later zero-lag-in-passband variant.
nodes.outputs: Smoothed line or band-limited oscillator.
nodes.repaints: no - causal IIR filter
nodes.weaknesses: A filter, not a strategy; no evidence of trading edge by itself. Improves signal-to-noise inputs for other rules.

nodes.name: Ehlers Dominant Cycle (Autocorrelation Periodogram / Hilbert period)
nodes.source: John Ehlers ('Cycle Analytics for Traders' ch. 8, 2013); TradingView ports by loxx, blackcat, mihakralj
nodes.what_it_does: Estimates the current dominant cycle period of price so other indicators (RSI, stochastic, MA lengths) can be tuned adaptively. The autocorrelation periodogram is Ehlers' preferred method.
nodes.core_math: Pre-filter price with a roofing filter; compute Pearson autocorrelation at lags 0..48 using a short averaging window (min 3 bars); take a DFT of the autocorrelation sequence to get power per period (e.g. 10-48 bars); smooth and normalize power; dominant cycle = center of gravity of power over periods.
nodes.outputs: Dominant period value (often a heatmap of spectral power); feeds adaptive lengths.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Markets are only intermittently cyclic; period estimates wander. No independent evidence that cycle-adaptive lengths beat fixed ones after costs.

nodes.name: Ehlers Fisher Transform (and Inverse Fisher Transform)
nodes.source: John Ehlers (S&C V.20:11, Nov 2002); TradingView built-in
nodes.what_it_does: Converts a bounded normalized price (or oscillator) into a near-Gaussian distribution so extremes become sharp, rare spikes that mark potential turning points. The Inverse Fisher compresses an oscillator (e.g. RSI) toward +/-1 for crisp threshold signals.
nodes.core_math: Normalize hl2 over n bars to [-1, 1] (x = 2 x (price - LL)/(HH - LL) - 1, smoothed and clamped to +/-0.999). Fisher = 0.5 ln((1+x)/(1-x)), then smoothed; signal line = Fisher[1]. Inverse Fisher: (e^(2y) - 1)/(e^(2y) + 1) on a scaled oscillator y.
nodes.outputs: Fisher line and trigger; crosses near extremes as reversal signals.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: The Gaussian claim is about the transformed indicator, not about returns being predictable; signals are frequent and noisy in trends. No robust independent evidence.

nodes.name: Hull Moving Average / Hull Suite
nodes.what_it_does: A low-lag moving average built from weighted moving averages; the Hull Suite packages HMA with EHMA and THMA variants, trend coloring, bands and a higher-timeframe option. One of the most widely used community trend overlays.
nodes.core_math: HMA(n) = WMA(2 x WMA(n/2) - WMA(n), sqrt(n)). EHMA substitutes EMAs; THMA = WMA(3 x WMA(n/3) - WMA(n/2) - WMA(n), n). Trend color by comparing the Hull value to its value 2 bars earlier.
nodes.outputs: Colored Hull line or band; flip alerts.
nodes.repaints: conditional - no on chart timeframe; the higher-timeframe mode can repaint if requested without lookahead-safe offsets
nodes.weaknesses: Low lag comes with overshoot and frequent color flips. No evidence of edge.

nodes.name: Kalman Filter price smoother
nodes.source: Rudolf Kalman (1960); community scripts e.g. BackQuant, Zeiierman, ChartPrime (TradingView)
nodes.what_it_does: Recursively estimates a hidden 'true' price (and optionally velocity) from noisy observations, balancing trust in the model vs. new data via process and measurement noise settings. Used as a responsive, low-lag trend line or as a smoother for oscillators.
nodes.core_math: Predict: x_pred = F x_prev, P_pred = F P F' + Q. Update: K = P_pred H' (H P_pred H' + R)^-1; x = x_pred + K (price - H x_pred); P = (I - K H) P_pred. Scalar versions use F=H=1 (random-walk level); two-state versions track level and slope.
nodes.outputs: Filtered price line, sometimes slope/trend state.
nodes.repaints: no - causal (only smoother/RTS variants use future data)
nodes.weaknesses: Behaviour hinges on Q/R choices, which are usually hand-tuned rather than estimated; with constant Q/R it reduces to an EMA-like filter. No evidence of edge by itself.

nodes.name: Volumatic Variable Index Dynamic Average [BigBeluga] (VIDYA)
nodes.license: TradingView House Rules (open-source; header license unknown)
nodes.what_it_does: Uses Chande's VIDYA (an EMA whose speed scales with the absolute Chande Momentum Oscillator) with ATR bands for trend flips, then accumulates buy vs. sell volume within each trend leg and marks pivot-based liquidity levels with their volume.
nodes.core_math: VIDYA_t = alpha x |CMO(m)| x price + (1 - alpha x |CMO(m)|) x VIDYA_{t-1}, alpha = 2/(n+1). Bands = VIDYA +/- k x ATR; trend flips when price crosses the band. During each trend, volume on up-candles vs. down-candles is summed into a delta readout. Pivot highs/lows are drawn as levels labeled with volume.
nodes.outputs: VIDYA line/bands, flip triangles, trend delta volume, pivot levels.
nodes.repaints: conditional - pivot levels confirm only after the pivot's right-side bars; VIDYA itself does not repaint
nodes.weaknesses: Candle-color volume split is a rough proxy. No evidence of edge.

nodes.name: Machine Learning: Lorentzian Classification
nodes.license: MPL-2.0 (per script header; TradingView House Rules for republication)
nodes.what_it_does: An approximate nearest-neighbor classifier that compares the current bar's feature vector (normalized RSI, WaveTrend, CCI, ADX variants) to history using Lorentzian distance, and votes on whether price will be higher or lower a fixed number of bars ahead. Optional volatility, regime and ADX filters plus a Nadaraya-Watson kernel trend gate the signals. The most-boosted ML script on TradingView.
nodes.core_math: Features: up to 5 normalized oscillators. Label for training bar = sign of price change 4 bars later. Distance = sum over features of ln(1 + |f_i - f_i_hist|). Scan a lookback (default 2000 bars) sampling every 4th bar; keep a list of up to k (default 8) neighbors whose distance exceeds a running threshold (chronological spacing, not strict k-NN); prediction = sum of neighbor labels. Filters: volatility (short vs. long ATR), regime (slope of a filtered price curve vs threshold), ADX; optional EMA/SMA and kernel-regression trend confirmation.
nodes.outputs: Prediction value, colored bars, buy/sell labels, kernel line, backtest stats table.
nodes.timeframes: Author states defaults optimized for 4H-12H; commonly misapplied intraday
nodes.repaints: no - author states no repainting once a bar closes (live bar may change)
nodes.weaknesses: In-sample stats table is not a proper walk-forward test; 'ANN' is a heuristic neighbor selection; label horizon and features are hand-picked. No independent out-of-sample evidence of edge; results are highly setting-dependent.

nodes.name: Nadaraya-Watson: Rational Quadratic Kernel (Non-Repainting)
nodes.license: MPL-2.0 (per script header; TradingView House Rules for republication)
nodes.what_it_does: A causal kernel-regression trend line: each point is a weighted average of past prices with weights given by a rational-quadratic kernel, closer bars weighted more. Unlike the popular repainting 'envelope' versions, it uses only past data so historical values stay fixed.
nodes.core_math: Estimate_t = sum_i w_i x price_{t-i} / sum_i w_i over i = 0..lookback (starting at a regression start bar), with w_i = (1 + i^2 / (2 alpha h^2))^(-alpha): h = bandwidth, alpha = relative weighting of scales (large alpha approaches Gaussian). Signals from slope change or from crossover of two estimates with different lags (a 'smoothed' Gaussian companion).
nodes.outputs: Kernel estimate line colored by slope; optional crossover signals.
nodes.repaints: no - author designed it to be non-repainting
nodes.weaknesses: Functionally a well-shaped weighted moving average; 'regression' labeling overstates novelty. No evidence of edge.

nodes.name: Machine Learning: kNN (capissimo)
nodes.what_it_does: Applies k-nearest-neighbors to recent price windows to predict the next value/direction. The 'New Approach' version is described by the author as approximating an SMA(20) curve at about N=17 while hinting at next-bar direction; related capissimo scripts use indicator values as features for a kNN strategy.
nodes.core_math: Build training records of consecutive prices (e.g. 9 predictors + 1 target); distance = absolute difference (1-D) or Euclidean over features; select neighbors at or below the K-th smallest distance; prediction = average of their targets (regression) or majority vote of direction (classification variants).
nodes.outputs: Prediction curve and/or directional signals.
nodes.repaints: unknown - not documented on the page
nodes.weaknesses: Author's own note that it approximates an SMA suggests little beyond smoothing. No out-of-sample evidence.

nodes.name: Logistic Regression (capissimo)
nodes.what_it_does: An experimental in-Pine logistic regression that estimates the probability of an up vs. down move and turns it into buy/sell signals. Widely copied and ported (e.g. to ThinkOrSwim).
nodes.core_math: Generic mechanism: fit weights by gradient descent over a rolling lookback to minimize log-loss of sigmoid(w . x) against binary up/down labels, then threshold the predicted probability. Exact features, labels and training schedule in capissimo's code are not documented on the page - unknown.
nodes.outputs: Probability/loss plot and signals (details unknown).
nodes.repaints: unknown - not documented; multi-timeframe option may repaint
nodes.weaknesses: Page documentation is minimal; mechanism details must be read from code. No evidence of edge.

nodes.name: Machine Learning Adaptive SuperTrend [AlgoAlpha]
nodes.license: TradingView House Rules (open-source; header license unknown)
nodes.what_it_does: Runs k-means clustering on ATR values over a training window to classify volatility into high/medium/low clusters, then feeds the current cluster's centroid ATR into a SuperTrend, so band width adapts to the volatility regime.
nodes.core_math: Compute ATR over a training period; initialize three centroids from user percentile guesses (e.g. 75/50/25th percentile of ATR); iterate assign-to-nearest-centroid and recompute means until stable; assign current ATR to its cluster; SuperTrend = hl2 +/- factor x centroid ATR with standard ratchet/flip logic.
nodes.outputs: Adaptive SuperTrend line, trend-flip triangles, table of centroids/cluster sizes/current regime.
nodes.repaints: unknown - not stated; clustering uses past data so likely no
nodes.weaknesses: 'ML' is 1-D k-means on ATR - equivalent to a percentile-based volatility bucket. No evidence of edge beyond standard Supertrend.

nodes.name: Hurst Exponent (R/S analysis)
nodes.what_it_does: Estimates long memory: H > 0.5 suggests persistent/trending behavior, H < 0.5 anti-persistent/mean-reverting, ~0.5 random walk. Used as a regime switch between trend and mean-reversion logic.
nodes.core_math: Over a lookback N of returns, split into subsamples of size N/2, N/4, N/8...; for each compute rescaled range R/S = (max - min of cumulative mean-adjusted sum)/stdev; average per size; H = slope of log(R/S) vs log(size). Simple versions use log(R/S)/log(n) on one window.
nodes.outputs: Hurst value oscillator around 0.5.
nodes.timeframes: All; needs long windows to be stable
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: R/S is biased in small samples (Anis-Lloyd correction exists) and very noisy on short intraday windows; confidence intervals around 0.5 are wide. No robust evidence that rolling Hurst improves trading after costs.

nodes.name: Choppiness Index (CHOP)
nodes.what_it_does: A non-directional regime gauge comparing the sum of bar ranges to the net high-low span: high readings mean price is churning sideways, low readings mean it is traveling efficiently.
nodes.core_math: CHOP = 100 x log10( sum(TR, n) / (highest high(n) - lowest low(n)) ) / log10(n), default n = 14; conventional thresholds 61.8 (choppy) and 38.2 (trending).
nodes.outputs: 0-100 oscillator with threshold lines.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Fibonacci thresholds are arbitrary. No academic evidence; useful as a filter.

nodes.name: Efficiency Ratio (Kaufman)
nodes.what_it_does: Ratio of net price change to the total path length over n bars; near 1 = straight-line trend, near 0 = noise. Drives KAMA and works as a standalone trend/chop regime filter.
nodes.core_math: ER = |close - close[n]| / sum_{i=0..n-1} |close[i] - close[i+1]|. Signed variant keeps the numerator's sign for direction.
nodes.outputs: 0-1 value (or -1..1 signed).
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Sensitive to n; single-number summary ignores volatility level. No standalone evidence of edge.

nodes.name: Volatility Regime / Volatility Targeting
nodes.source: Moreira & Muir, Journal of Finance (2017); common quant practice
nodes.what_it_does: Classifies the market by realized volatility (e.g. short vs. long ATR ratio, realized-vol percentile, VIX level) and scales exposure inversely to it. Moreira & Muir show taking less risk when volatility is high raises Sharpe ratios for the market and many factors because volatility changes are not offset by proportional expected-return changes.
nodes.core_math: Realized vol sigma_t (e.g. stdev of returns over last 20 days or EWMA); position weight = target_vol / sigma_t (capped). Regime flags: ATR(short)/ATR(long) > 1 = expanding; percentile rank of sigma_t over 1 year.
nodes.outputs: Regime label and position scalar.
nodes.timeframes: Daily evidence; intraday analogues via intraday realized vol
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Later work (e.g. Cederburg et al. 2020, 'On the performance of volatility-managed portfolios') finds out-of-sample gains are weaker and inconsistent across factors. Strong evidence for risk control, mixed for alpha.

nodes.name: Range Filter [DW]
nodes.what_it_does: A step-like filter line that only moves when price exceeds a smoothed-range threshold from the current filter value, ignoring moves smaller than the threshold. Produces clean trend states and target bands; one of the most-copied community trend filters (base of many 'Range Filter Buy and Sell' scripts).
nodes.core_math: Range size r from a chosen method (ATR, average change, stdev, points, %, ticks) x multiplier, optionally smoothed. Filter_t = Filter_{t-1} unless price (close or wicks) moves beyond Filter_{t-1} +/- r, in which case filter moves to price -/+ r. Direction = sign of filter change; target bands = filter +/- r. Optional conditional EMA averaging of samples on filter changes.
nodes.outputs: Filter line, target bands, colored bars, external +1/-1 output.
nodes.repaints: no on closed bars (not documented explicitly); wick-based source can flip intrabar
nodes.weaknesses: Still a lagging trend filter; threshold choice drives everything. No evidence of edge.

nodes.name: Rolling Z-Score of Price
nodes.source: Statistics classic; many TradingView scripts (e.g. BigBeluga Z Score Overlay)
nodes.what_it_does: Standardizes price's distance from a rolling mean in units of rolling standard deviation, giving a scale-free overbought/oversold measure for mean-reversion entries. Equivalent in shape to Bollinger %b.
nodes.core_math: z = (close - SMA(close, n)) / stdev(close, n). Variants apply it to VWAP distance, returns, or spreads; entries at |z| > 2, exits near 0.
nodes.outputs: Z oscillator with threshold lines.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Assumes stationarity; in trends z stays extreme. No edge by itself; relevant only where mean reversion is established (e.g. short-horizon index reversal - see IBS/RSI2 nodes).

nodes.name: Linear Regression Channel
nodes.source: Statistics classic; TradingView built-in Linear Regression / Regression Trend tool
nodes.what_it_does: Fits a least-squares line to the last n closes and draws bands at multiples of the residual standard deviation, with Pearson's R showing how linear the trend is. Used for trend slope, mean reversion to the fit line, and channel breakouts.
nodes.core_math: Slope and intercept from OLS of close on bar index over n; center = fitted line; upper/lower = center +/- k x stdev of residuals (or max deviation); Pearson R measures fit quality.
nodes.outputs: Center line, deviation bands, Pearson's R.
nodes.repaints: yes - the whole fitted line is redrawn each bar over the window; only the endpoint series (linreg value) is non-repainting
nodes.weaknesses: Visual channel repaints and misleads backtests; no evidence of edge.

nodes.name: Mean-Reversion Half-Life (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck)
nodes.what_it_does: Estimates how fast a series (price minus VWAP, spread, z-score) reverts to its mean by fitting an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck/AR(1) model. The half-life sets lookback length, holding time and time stops for mean-reversion trades, and a non-negative estimated speed flags that the series is not mean-reverting.
nodes.core_math: Regress delta y_t on y_{t-1}: delta y_t = a + lambda x y_{t-1} + e. If lambda < 0, half-life = -ln(2)/lambda (equivalently with phi = AR(1) coefficient, half-life = -ln 2 / ln phi); long-run mean = -a/lambda.
nodes.outputs: Half-life in bars, mean, reversion speed.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Small-sample bias makes reversion look faster than it is; parameters are unstable across regimes. A diagnostic, not a signal.

nodes.name: Internal Bar Strength (IBS)
nodes.source: Pagonidis, 'The IBS Effect: Mean Reversion in Equity ETFs' (NAAIM, 2013)
nodes.what_it_does: Where the close sits within the bar's range. For US equity indices, closes near the low (IBS < 0.2) have tended to be followed by next-day gains and closes near the high by weaker returns - a daily mean-reversion effect Pagonidis documents as strong and consistent since the late 1990s.
nodes.core_math: IBS = (close - low) / (high - low), in [0,1]. Classic rule: buy at close when IBS < 0.2 (often with a trend or RSI filter), exit next close or when IBS > 0.8.
nodes.outputs: 0-1 value; entry/exit thresholds.
nodes.repaints: no (final only at bar close)
nodes.weaknesses: Pagonidis reports alpha before transaction costs and notes costs greatly erode it; a practitioner/white-paper study, not peer-reviewed, though widely replicated by practitioners on SPY/QQQ and by a 2023 arXiv study on country ETFs. Effect may have decayed with publicity.

nodes.name: RSI(2) Mean Reversion (Connors)
nodes.source: Larry Connors & Cesar Alvarez, 'Short Term Trading Strategies That Work' (2008)
nodes.what_it_does: Buys short-term oversold pullbacks inside a long-term uptrend using a 2-period RSI, exploiting short-horizon mean reversion in US equity indices. Published backtests show high win rates (~75%+) with 1-3 day holds.
nodes.core_math: Wilder RSI with length 2. Long when close > SMA(200) and RSI(2) < 10 (or < 5); exit when close > SMA(5). Mirror for shorts below SMA(200) with RSI(2) > 90/95.
nodes.outputs: Entry/exit signals.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Evidence is author/practitioner backtests, not peer-reviewed; left-tail risk when pullbacks become crashes (no stop in classic rules). Short-horizon index reversal itself is consistent with IBS findings. Intraday transfer unproven.

nodes.name: UT Bot Alerts
nodes.source: QuantNomad (TradingView); original idea Yo_adriiiiaan, based on HPotter
nodes.what_it_does: An ATR trailing stop with buy/sell alerts when price crosses it, optionally computed on Heikin Ashi closes. Among the most-used community signal scripts, frequently paired with the Range Filter or STC in retail systems.
nodes.core_math: nLoss = key value x ATR(c). Trailing stop ratchets: if price and prior price are above the prior stop, stop = max(prior stop, price - nLoss); if both below, stop = min(prior stop, price + nLoss); otherwise reset to price -/+ nLoss depending on side. Buy when price crosses above stop (EMA(1) of source vs stop), sell when crosses below.
nodes.outputs: Trailing stop line, buy/sell labels, alerts.
nodes.repaints: no on standard candles; with Heikin Ashi source, signals do not match tradable prices
nodes.weaknesses: Essentially an ATR trailing stop (Supertrend/Chandelier cousin); viral backtests usually use HA prices or no costs. No credible evidence of edge.

nodes.name: WaveTrend Oscillator [WT]
nodes.source: LazyBear (TradingView port of a TS/MT indicator)
nodes.what_it_does: A smoothed, CCI-like momentum oscillator with a signal line; crosses in overbought/oversold zones are used as reversal signals. It is the core of Market Cipher B / VuManChu Cipher B and a feature in jdehorty's Lorentzian classifier.
nodes.core_math: ap = hlc3; esa = EMA(ap, n1); d = EMA(|ap - esa|, n1); ci = (ap - esa) / (0.015 x d); wt1 = EMA(ci, n2); wt2 = SMA(wt1, 4). Defaults n1 = 10, n2 = 21; OB/OS levels around +/-53 to +/-60.
nodes.outputs: wt1, wt2, histogram of difference, OB/OS lines.
nodes.repaints: no
nodes.weaknesses: Standard oscillator behavior: stays pinned in trends, many false reversals. No published evidence of edge.

nodes.name: VuManChu Cipher B + Divergences
nodes.source: VuManChu (TradingView), inspired by commercial Market Cipher B
nodes.what_it_does: A composite oscillator panel combining WaveTrend, an RSI+MFI money-flow area, Stochastic RSI and automatic divergence detection, with colored dots marking WaveTrend crosses. One of the most-used free community composites, especially in crypto.
nodes.core_math: WaveTrend (as in LazyBear) for waves and cross dots; a money-flow proxy from a smoothed candle-body/range measure (labelled RSI+MFI area); Stoch RSI; divergence detection by comparing fractal (pivot) highs/lows of the oscillator with those of price. Exact money-flow formula not verified.
nodes.outputs: Wave lines, money-flow area, green/red/gold dots, divergence lines.
nodes.repaints: conditional - divergence and fractal marks are drawn after pivot confirmation bars
nodes.weaknesses: Many overlapping signals invite cherry-picking; no evidence of edge.

nodes.name: Pivot Point SuperTrend
nodes.license: TradingView House Rules (open-source; header indicates MPL-2.0 - unverified)
nodes.what_it_does: A SuperTrend whose center line is a weighted running average of confirmed pivot highs/lows instead of hl2, making bands follow market structure. Includes an optional centerline for early exits and pivot-based S/R.
nodes.core_math: Detect pivot highs/lows with period p (default 2); center = (center x 2 + new pivot) / 3 on each new pivot (weighted smoothing); bands = center +/- factor x ATR(n) with SuperTrend ratchet/flip rules.
nodes.outputs: Trend line, buy/sell labels, centerline, pivot S/R.
nodes.repaints: no - pivots enter the center only once confirmed (introducing p bars of lag)
nodes.weaknesses: Supertrend-family whipsaw; no evidence of edge.

nodes.name: Range Oscillator (Zeiierman)
nodes.license: TradingView House Rules (open-source; header license unknown)
nodes.what_it_does: Detects an adaptive price range (ATR-scaled) around a volatility-weighted equilibrium and normalizes price's distance from it to +/-100, with a heatmap showing how often price has interacted with each zone. Aims to separate ranging from breaking-out conditions.
nodes.core_math: Range width = ATR x width multiplier, validated by a minimum bar count; equilibrium = weighted mean where larger bar-to-bar changes get more weight; oscillator = (price - equilibrium) / range half-width x 100. Heat levels from touch frequency. Exact weighting formula not verified.
nodes.outputs: Oscillator with +/-100 boundaries, heatmap coloring, trend-shift transitions.
nodes.repaints: unknown - not documented
nodes.weaknesses: Recent script with no track record; no evidence of edge.

dimensions.trend: Direction and persistence of price movement (moving averages, supertrend, regression slope).
dimensions.momentum: Speed or acceleration of price change (RSI, MACD, rate of change, oscillators).
dimensions.volatility: Size of price ranges and their expansion or contraction (ATR, bands, squeezes).
dimensions.market_structure: Sequence of swing highs and lows, and breaks of them (BOS, CHoCH, pivots).
dimensions.liquidity: Where resting stop orders likely sit and whether they were swept (equal highs/lows, prior highs/lows, stop hunts).
dimensions.imbalance_zones: Price areas left inefficient or where large orders originated (FVGs, order blocks, supply/demand).
dimensions.volume_flow: Traded volume, its distribution across price, or buy/sell pressure (volume profile, VWAP, delta).
dimensions.time_session: Time-of-day or calendar effects (killzones, session opens, opening range).
dimensions.mean_reversion: Statistical stretch away from a fair value and the pull back to it (z-score, channels, kernels).
dimensions.regime: Whether the market is trending or ranging, or which volatility state it is in (Hurst, choppiness, efficiency ratio).

roles.filter: Allows or blocks trading based on market condition or time, without choosing direction.
roles.bias: Sets the directional context or higher-timeframe bias; decides which side to trade.
roles.location: Marks where to look for a trade: a price level or zone of interest.
roles.trigger: Fires the precise entry moment on a specific bar.
roles.risk: Places stops, targets, trailing exits or position size.

relations.duplicate: They compute essentially the same thing; using both adds nothing.
relations.alternative: Different methods for the same job in a trade; a system would pick one of them.
relations.precondition: `a` must happen or be checked first, and `b` only makes sense after it (a feeds into b).
relations.follows: `b` must happen or be checked first, and `a` only makes sense after it (b feeds into a).
relations.confirming: Independent evidence for the same signal at the same moment; agreement raises confidence.
relations.gating: One of them decides when or whether the other should be used, without choosing direction.
relations.conflicting: They rest on incompatible assumptions or typically signal opposite actions.
